name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills district, a pine-covered hill station at about 1,500 m elevation known as the Scotland of the East. Colonial architecture, markets, lakes, and base for exploring Khasi Hills attractions.

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest peak in Meghalaya at about 1,965 m, located ~10 km south of Shillong. Offers panoramic views of the city, hills, and distant plains; sacred to Khasi people as abode of deity Lei Shyllong. Access controlled near Air Force installation.
facts: Sacred to Khasi as dwelling of Lei Shyllong
Photo ID required; cameras restricted at gate

name: Elephant Falls
description: Multi-tiered waterfall on the outskirts of Shillong (Upper Shillong), originally known in Khasi as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew (three-step waterfall). Cascades over fern-covered rocks; popular short stop en route to Cherrapunji.
facts: About 12 km from Shillong city centre
Khasi name: Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew
Named after a rock resembling an elephant (destroyed in 1897 quake)

name: Ward's Lake
description: Man-made lake in the heart of Shillong, named after Sir William Ward. Features a walking path, gardens, and boating; a popular local recreational spot known locally as Nan Polok.
facts: Named after Sir William Ward, Chief Commissioner of Assam
Gardens and footpaths around the lake

name: Don Bosco Museum (Centre for Indigenous Cultures)
description: Seven-storey museum in Mawlai, Shillong, dedicated to the indigenous cultures of Northeast India. Houses extensive galleries on tribes, textiles, tools, and a skywalk offering city views.

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Historic town on the southern Khasi Hills plateau, once recorded as the wettest place on Earth. Gateway to living root bridges, dramatic waterfalls, caves, and views over Bangladesh plains. Officially Sohra; elevation ~1,430 m.
facts: Holds records for highest rainfall in a month and year
Base for root bridges and Nohkalikai Falls

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India (~340 m / 1,115 ft), plunging from the Cherrapunji/Sohra plateau into a green pool. Fed by short streams on the plateau; dramatic views especially in monsoon. Linked to local legend of Ka Likai.
facts: Tallest plunge waterfall in India (~340 m)
Plunge pool with distinctive green water

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-tier living root bridge in Nongriat village, grown from Ficus elastica roots guided by Khasi people over generations. Requires a steep trek of ~3,000–3,500 steps down from Tyrna; one of the most famous bioengineered structures in the world.
facts: Located in Nongriat village, East Khasi Hills
Two stacked tiers of living roots
Estimated age of lower bridge over 180 years

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Khasi village in Pynursla block near the Bangladesh border, long celebrated as one of Asia’s cleanest villages. Features traditional bamboo houses, living root bridge nearby, skywalk, and community-driven cleanliness with bamboo dustbins everywhere.
facts: Awarded cleanest village in Asia (Discover India, 2003)

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic clifftop viewpoint and canyon in East Khasi Hills, about 25 km from Shillong near Smit. Offers sweeping views of deep green gorges and valleys; steep trail descends to Rasong village. Popular for sunrise/sunset photography.
facts: Steep steps down to Rasong village
Best at sunrise or sunset for cloud seas

name: Mawphlang Sacred Grove
description: Ancient sacred forest (Law Lyngdoh) near Mawphlang village, protected for centuries by Khasi tradition. Visitors must take nothing out; features monoliths, old trees, and biodiversity. Guided walks only; ~25 km from Shillong.
facts: Protected by community taboo: nothing may be removed
Contains ancient monoliths and coronation sites
One of the best-known sacred groves in Meghalaya

name: Kongthong Village (Whistling Village)
description: Remote Khasi village in East Khasi Hills famous for the unique whistled language (Jingrwai Lawbei) where each person has a personal tune composed by their mother. Surrounded by hills, living root bridges nearby, and traditional homestays.
facts: India’s entry for UNWTO Best Tourism Villages
